MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The step drill bits fit a clear next task: enlarging sheet-metal holes for the rivets and rivet nuts I have been buying.",
    "The truss-head screws and fender washers complement my fastening supplies by helping secure thin panels and spread clamping force.",
    "Disposable gloves connect to my epoxy and adhesive work, provided their chemical compatibility suits the material I am using."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The pressure gauge is a repair tool, but I have no current task requiring its pressure range or connection size.",
    "Anatomy models and merchandise bags do not support the drilling, fastening, mounting, and repair tasks reflected in my recent purchases.",
    "The extra screw assortment fits my interests but overlaps supplies I already own; the truss-head screws offer a more specific reason to buy now.",
    "The glue interests me for quick repairs, but the conflicting cyanoacrylate and epoxy wording leaves me unsure whether it suits the job."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in workshop equipment seems to have been stretched into interest in any repair instrument, even when it serves an unrelated task.",
    "Repeated fastener purchases seem to be treated as a continuing need for more assortments, without enough attention to what a new set adds."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "I am most interested in supplies that work with tools and hardware I already have, such as step bits for rivet holes and washers for bolts.",
    "Dimensions, materials, and intended use matter: eye hooks can be relevant without being worth buying before I know the anchor size and load needed.",
    "Frequent workshop purchases do not mean I need every related item immediately; a specific project or a useful capability I lack gives me a stronger reason to choose."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations recognized my workshop interests, but matched me best when they extended a specific task rather than simply adding more tools or fasteners."
}
